scoring_justification: MAE and relative error are recomputed from the agent's raw CSV and text files against hidden reference values derived from the paper's simulation data and theoretical expression.

hidden_assets.purpose: gold magnetization values and G coefficient
hidden_assets.source_provenance: paper's reported simulation points (m=0.93,0.89,0.86 at t/τ=0.1,0.3,0.5) and extrapolation / theoretical expression Eq. (6.20)
hidden_assets.generation_method: the three known points were taken from the paper's text; the remaining three were estimated by fitting an exponent of 0.46 as reported in the paper's short-time analysis (Fig. 10). The theoretical G is directly computed from the paper's Eq. (6.20) with α = 16π/(9√3) and the given parameters.
hidden_assets.why_not_fabricated: the three time points are explicitly stated in the paper; the extrapolation is based on the paper's own best-fit exponent of 0.46, and the theoretical G is an exact closed-form expression from the paper's derived rate equations, not an arbitrary number.

outputs.description: Averaged magnetization m(t) at six normalized times; the checker recomputes the mean absolute error against hidden paper‑reported values for these same conditions and scores monotonically (lower error yields higher reward).

Fitted coefficient G from the short‑time sqrt(t) law; the checker computes the relative error with respect to the paper‑derived theoretical coefficient and scores monotonically (smaller relative error yields higher reward).

output_contract.notes: The agent must implement the Monte Carlo simulation from scratch using the public protocol and parameters. No gold values are given; the checker compares against hidden reference values derived from the paper's own simulation and theoretical expression.

steps.description: Mean absolute error between agent's reported magnetization points and hidden reference values derived from the paper's simulation.
Relative error between the agent's fitted G and the theoretical dimensionless coefficient Γ_{1/2}τ = 9√3/(16π²) ≈ 0.098699.
